title: Spruce Logistics - stress and economics sprint (benchmark notes)
content:
Purpose:
Run a short focused sprint to characterize: steady-state throughput, tail latency under mixed QPS bursts, and $/1M-token cost tradeoffs for Spruce Logistics’ recommended inference topology. This is an internal working note (notes-to-self style) — results will feed the customer workshop on 2026-04-22.

Scope and goals:
- Workloads: short chat-like queries (avg 40 tokens output), longer summarization (avg 400 tokens), and embedding-only calls for retrieval (512-d).
- Targets: identify configurations that meet p95 < 150ms for short queries, p99 < 500ms where practical, and quantify cost per 1M tokens for each config.
- Compare: Hosted single-model (gptx-7b-like FP16), Dedicated pooled GPUs (A100-80GB family), and a quantized private variant (int4) on dedicated nodes.

Environment details (test harness):
- Harness: locust-based generator + internal replay tool to mimic real traffic (interarrival distribution copied from Spruce telemetry).
- Dataset: 10k sampled requests from production-like traces (anonymized).
- Measurement: microsecond-precision timing, token counters from runtime, and exporter metrics scraped every 5s.
- Warmup: 30 minutes of low QPS, then 15-minute ramp to steady-state.

Configurations tested (short labels used later):
- H-FP16: Hosted API, model baseline, FP16, default batching (window 25ms), KV caching enabled.
- D-A100-FP16: Dedicated pool (2x A100-80), FP16, queue depth tuned to target 80% GPU util.
- D-A100-INT4: Dedicated pool with int4 quantized build, compile flags to fastrun, reduced sequence-kernel tolerance.
- Fallback policy: when latency > 900ms fallback to smaller model (gptx-3b) — used in a subset of runs to measure graceful degradation.

Key quantitative summary (closed-book highlights):
- Short chat (40 tokens output):
  - H-FP16: p50=30ms, p95=140ms, p99=420ms, throughput ~95 req/s, estimated cost = $18 / 1M output tokens.
  - D-A100-FP16: p50=18ms, p95=85ms, p99=210ms, throughput ~260 req/s, estimated cost = $6.8 / 1M output tokens.
  - D-A100-INT4: p50=16ms, p95=78ms, p99=190ms, throughput ~300 req/s, estimated cost = $4.9 / 1M output tokens.
- Long summarization (400 tokens):
  - H-FP16: p50=520ms, p95=1.6s, p99=2.8s, throughput ~6.5 req/s, cost ~= $220 / 1M output tokens.
  - D-A100-FP16: p50=220ms, p95=640ms, p99=1.1s, throughput ~25 req/s, cost ~= $83 / 1M tokens.
  - D-A100-INT4: p50=200ms, p95=580ms, p99=980ms, throughput ~30 req/s, cost ~= $59 / 1M tokens.
- Embedding-only: similar relative improvements; int4 shows negligible degradation vs FP16 for embedding vectors but reduces memory and increases concurrent endpoints by ~18%.

Observations and unusual behaviors (raw notes):
- Cold-start microbursts: Hosted service saw large p99 spikes (up to 1.8s) during the first two minutes after a 2000-rps burst — likely scheduler scaling/queue spillover. Dedicated pools with prewarmed instances did not show the same magnitude spike.
- KV cache hit patterns: For chat flows, cache hit ratio ~28% (prefix reuse across sessions). Increasing cache retention to 10min gave modest latency drops but increased memory pressure; int4 builds had slightly less headroom for KV due to smaller per-kv packing semantics.
- Batching window tradeoff: Increasing window 25ms->50ms improved throughput ~12% but added ~20ms median latency on short queries; for Spruce use-case median is important (UX requires snappy), so default 25ms recommended for hosted-like tiers.
- Quantization artifacts: int4 produced occasional token-level stop-early behavior in long summarization (observed 3/1200 long runs). Post-hoc inspection shows softmax tail scaling difference; mitigation: enable per-layer calibration + fallback to fp16 for sequences > 1024 tokens.

Cost model notes (back-of-envelope):
- Cost includes GPU runtime, infra, and amortized model storage. Numbers above are rough; exact customer pricing will vary. Dedicated int4 shows ~28-32% cost savings relative to dedicated fp16 at similar SLOs. Hosted often trades higher unit cost for operational simplicity; recommend dedicated for sustained heavy workloads.

Experiment log (timeboxed runs):
- 2026-04-13 09:00: Full warmup, H-FP16 short chat baseline (3x 15m ramps). Noted occasional 500ms p99 blips at 10:15 (root cause: region routing failover event in cloud).
- 2026-04-13 13:30: D-A100-FP16 run. Tuned queue depth from 64->96 (GPU util target). Observed throughput increase but 95th tail rose slightly; reverted to 80.
- 2026-04-14 10:00: D-A100-INT4 compile with per-layer calibration. Run flagged 3 misbehaving summarization outputs; reproduced locally, added per-seq fallback.
- 2026-04-15 16:45: Mixed QPS test (sawtooth bursts 0->1200 rps every 120s). H-FP16 suffered queue spill and delayed autoscale. Dedicated pools sustained bursts with slightly increased p95 but within SLO.

Recommendations (what to propose to Spruce):
1) For production customer rollout (baseline): Dedicated A100 pool with int4 builds and per-sequence fallback to fp16 for sequences > 1024 tokens. This balances cost and SLOs; estimated starting commit: 4 GPUs per critical region.
2) Warm-start policy: prewarm a small number of nodes per region (2 nodes) to handle cold microbursts; revisit warm-up heuristics in the control plane.
3) KV cache tuning: keep default 5–10 minute retention but enable memory guardrails on int4 nodes.
4) Batching config per route: short-chat route use 20–30ms window; long-summaries use 60–100ms window and larger queue allowances.
5) Monitoring: add synthetic probes that ramp from 0->burst to catch autoscaling slowdowns; surface per-route p99 runbooks in Console.

Follow-ups and action items (owners):
- Diego M: produce a compact slide with the quantitative tables and cost curves for workshop (due 2026-04-19).
- Priya N: prepare the int4 calibration notes and create a short repo PR for the compile flags we used (due 2026-04-17).
- Ava (me): draft the customer-facing recommendation one-pager and migration checklist (due 2026-04-20).

Open questions to validate with Spruce before proposal:
- Expected steady-state QPS per region and peak burst profile (they provided approximate numbers but want to confirm weekend/holiday multipliers).
- Data residency constraints for embeddings — if they require on-prem for vector store, we need to re-evaluate cost model.
- SLA tolerance for p99 deviations (are occasional 800–1200ms spikes acceptable?).

Rough appendix (short):
- Commands used: ./bench/run --config spruce_short.json --replay-sample 10000 --emit-metrics prometheus
- Key metrics exported: redwood_runtime_request_latency_seconds{quantile}, redwood_tokens_generated_total, redwood_gpu_utilization_percent
- Artifact links: see linked_artifacts for PR + confluence.

Notes-to-self: pull a second pass on quantization artifacts — run a 10k long-summary-only sweep with and without per-layer calibration to build confidence before presenting. Also capture a short recording of the mixed-burst run for the workshop — the visual is convincing.

End of note.
